title: Thermodynamics of interacting magnetic chain molecules
abstract: We study magnets composed of molecules with an arbitrary number $m$ of magnetically active atoms in a chain configuration interacting with nearest-neighbor couplings. We derive the thermodynamics of a chain of spin-$j$ $SU(2)$ magnetic atoms using a mean-field approach and determine the equilibrium states and stability conditions. The system exhibits a rich phase structure with a cascade of ferromagnetic phase transitions, their number ranging from $m$, for maximal ferromagnets, to zero, for paramagnets, depending on the relative strengths of the couplings. In the presence of impurities (modified couplings) at the ends of the chain, boundary states emerge that coexist with the paramagnetic phase or the fully ferromagnetic phase. For long chains, a continuum approximation can be taken that clarifies the structure of the phases. In the continuum description, magnetized states at temperatures lower than the critical temperature at which they appear correspond to kink solitons.
summary: This work theoretically investigates the thermodynamics and phase transitions in magnetic chains built from multi-atom molecules. Using mean-field theory, the authors map out a complex phase diagram featuring multiple ferromagnetic transitions. The analysis also details the emergence of boundary states due to impurities, providing deep insights into the stability of magnetic order.
main_problem: The paper derives the thermodynamics and analyzes the rich phase structure of magnetic chains composed of molecules with an arbitrary number of interacting magnetic atoms.
main_result: The system exhibits a cascade of ferromagnetic phase transitions, and boundary states can emerge in the presence of impurities, characterized by critical temperatures.
method: The analysis employs the mean-field approach, utilizing the saddle point method to evaluate the partition function and determine equilibrium free energy and stability conditions.
model_or_system: The model consists of magnets built from molecules of $m$ magnetically active atoms in a chain, governed by an SU(N) invariant Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings.
key_observables: Order parameters ($x_s$), free energy ($F$), and critical temperatures ($T_k, T_B$).
important_parameters: Coupling constants ($C_{st}$), temperature ($T$), and the number of atoms in the molecule ($m$).
main_assumptions: The derivation of the equilibrium free energy relies on the mean-field approximation and the saddle point method; stability analysis is performed on the off-equilibrium free energy.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the general SU(N) ferromagnet Hamiltonian to the mean-field free energy, establishing equilibrium conditions, and then analyzing the stability and emergence of boundary states in the discrete chain model.
why_interesting: The study of phase transitions, critical phenomena, and the emergence of boundary modes in interacting quantum spin systems is fundamental to understanding magnetic materials and quantum many-body physics.
